# Houston and Phoenix lead South and West targets with high white space and low penetration.

| Rank | Metro | Category | Penetration | Opportunity | White Space |
|------|-------|----------|-------------|-------------|-------------|
| 1 | Houston | Food & Beverage Stores | 8% [F1] | 9.52 [F1] | $5.50B [F1] |
| 2 | Phoenix | Restaurants & Food Service | 6% [F2] | 8.65 [F2] | $2.88B [F2] |
| 3 | Denver | Food & Beverage Stores | 20% [F3] | 8.29 [F3] | $1.49B [F3] |
| 4 | Dallas | Food & Beverage Stores | 20% [F4] | 8.25 [F4] | $2.78B [F4] |
| 5 | Phoenix | Food & Beverage Stores | 21% [F5] | 8.18 [F5] | $3.49B [F5] |
| 6 | Los Angeles | Food & Beverage Stores | 24% [F6] | 7.87 [F6] | $7.71B [F6] |
| 7 | Atlanta | Food & Beverage Stores | 24% [F7] | 7.85 [F7] | $0.99B [F7] |
| 8 | Miami | Food & Beverage Stores | 25% [F8] | 7.80 [F8] | $0.92B [F8] |

* Houston Food & Beverage Stores combines the highest opportunity score (9.52 [F1]) with the lowest regional penetration (8% [F1]) and category growth of 10.35% [F1] over 24 months.
* Phoenix appears twice in the top 5: Restaurants & Food Service at 6% penetration [F2] and Food & Beverage Stores at 21% penetration [F5], together representing $6.4B in white space ($2.88B [F2] + $3.49B [F5]).
* Los Angeles holds the largest single white space pool at $7.71B [F6] but ranks sixth in opportunity score (7.87 [F6]) due to higher existing penetration (24% [F6]) compared to Houston and Phoenix.
